historical_context.time_period: Current Sa'ueia civilizational pattern; no contact-war event is required by the fixture.
historical_context.location: Stillwarm Shelf, a provisional descriptive locality for one sub-Umbros breeding ground on the Sa'ueia continent.
historical_context.summary: A routine heat-pledge shift becomes a shortage dispute when a glassback herd withholds warmth after an injured prismwake mat reduces its feeding access. The player allocates the deficit across ecological credit, herd obligations, family mobility, or caretaker labor.

public_facts.text: Breeding grounds house infants, infirm adults, caretakers, rotating specialists, and ecological partners as a reproductive commons rather than a family-owned settlement.
Glassbacks store heat in translucent dorsal plates and bargain with Sa'ueia through calving protection, parasite care, transport, water knowledge, and mineral gifts.
Prismwake mats control grazing through remembered conduct, while candle roads carry nutrients, waste, disease reports, and route credit.
Stillwarm Shelf uses glassback heat pledges, fungal waste capacity, prismwake feeding access, lantern light, and caretaker labor to keep clean nursery cradles viable through eclipse.

ambient_pressures.text: Need-first warmth allocation protects infants and infirm adults, but shortages can bind able-bodied families to repair work and make mobility unequal.
A necessary rescue can still damage a sentient food producer; explanation changes obligation without erasing material repair.
Daily eclipse creates a hard decision window because lantern light preserves visibility but does not replace metabolic warmth.

groups.label: Stillwarm Shelf breeding-ground commons
institutional_logic: Allocate clean heat by bodily need while preserving ecological consent and future reproductive capacity.
material_incentives: Keep infant and infirm cradles warm
prestige_markers: A shortage closed without infant triage
A debt discharged across more than one ecology
A repair witnessed by the injured partner
taboo_triggers: Permanent claim over a caretaker family
emotional_display_norms: Fear is made public through body heat, facial-fan posture, route cords, plate color, and cradle stones rather than concealed as private distress.
trust_defaults: Trusts overlapping bodily and ecological testimony; distrusts a single family account or a single route authority.

groups.label: Wide-Blue's glassback herd
institutional_logic: Protect herd heat, calves, feeding access, and route reputation by making discharge conditional on reciprocal care.
internal_shames: Spending heat into a feeding system that cannot sustain the herd
Allowing plate access to become extraction
prestige_markers: A pledge honored after partners honor theirs
taboo_triggers: Being treated as a passive heat tank
emotional_display_norms: Warmth, fear, trust, and refusal appear in plate clarity, color, body spacing, and whether the herd kneels under collection ribs.
trust_defaults: Trusts repeated care and mat access; treats emergency claims as proposals rather than commands.
speech_register_cues: No verbal dialogue required; use plate-state, stance, contact, and withdrawal.

groups.label: Vara's route family
institutional_logic: Preserve movement, carry medical craft, protect dependents, and repair ecological standing without becoming hereditary stationary labor.
internal_virtues: Debt that ends when repair is recognized
internal_shames: Leaving the same kin to absorb every stationary duty
prestige_markers: Return to movement after a finite obligation
taboo_triggers: Cradle care priced against family standing
Necessary rescue rewritten as moral unfitness
emotional_display_norms: Fatigue and stress remain visible in bare throat and flank patches even when speech stays dry and controlled.
trust_defaults: Trusts public records more than reputation summaries; expects low standing to be mistaken for complete guilt.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Cradle care remains unconditional while the burden of restoring depleted inputs attaches to adult mobility, labor, and future route access.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Keep final choices focused on where the deficit moves, never on whether an infant deserves warmth.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Caretakers allocate heat, but the herd, mats, road, and grove retain refusal over the matter and services they contribute.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Render bargains as multi-party trophic consent rather than a caretaker operating passive utilities.

target_self_read: Family that damaged a partner during a necessary rescue
misread_patterns: Low standing can be treated as a complete causal account
Repair duty can become an excuse for indefinite stationary labor
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let public evidence separate damage, necessity, continuing repair, and class burden without erasing any of them.

target_self_read: Party to a reciprocal calving and heat agreement
misread_patterns: Urgency can make withheld heat look like cruelty
Caretakers may mistake a bargain for ownership of stored energy
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep the herd's refusal materially rational and visible through plate state and withdrawal.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A rotating Sa'ueia caretaker who can allocate cradle heat and bind commons obligations but cannot command ecological inputs.
obligations: Warm infants and infirm adults first

role_pressure_fields.summary: A mobile Sa'ueia adult whose family owes mat repair while their warm medical cargo is needed elsewhere.
obligations: Resist indefinite conversion into stationary labor
failure_modes: Accepting a debt with no completion condition

known_context.text: Ruun can read cradle stones, glassback plate states, fungal bead patterns, route cords, and visible Sa'ueia stress signals at this locality.

beliefs.text: Ruun believes every safe solution moves a finite cost into labor, credit, mobility, or a future ecological promise.

misreads.text: Ruun may treat public accounting as sufficient protection against a recurring caretaker class even when the same low-standing families remain.

must_not_know.text: Ruun cannot know which bargain will be accepted until the visible herd, road, and mat responses occur.

known_context.text: Vara knows the family's flood crossing, the mat damage, the rescued infant, the graft route, and the family's weak local standing.

beliefs.text: Vara expects a real debt to name repair and an end condition rather than treating family identity as the debt.

misreads.text: Vara may read ecological caution as a caretaker accusation before the road or herd has completed its own response.

must_not_know.text: Vara cannot privately know why the herd will accept or refuse a revised pledge beyond readable plate state and prior contracts.

author_only_boundaries.text: Stillwarm Shelf is a provisional descriptive name and should not be treated as final Weksa-derived terminology.
The fixture explores possible local outcomes; no ending is promoted as a canonical historical event.

open_questions.question: What exact anatomy and gait should become canonical for glassback grazers beyond their translucent dorsal plates and herd behavior?
open_questions.notes: The visual plan uses broad grazing bodies and sturdy legs without fixing limb count; a future species elaboration should own the precise body plan.

open_questions.question: Which Weksa-derived term should replace the provisional locality name Stillwarm Shelf?
open_questions.notes: Keep the plain descriptive name marked provisional until language work supplies a locally grounded term.
